title: Measure EFS metadata latency in-VPC before writing EFS CDK
description:
## Question

**Is EFS fast enough in-VPC for a hot working tree?**

D1 makes one EFS filesystem the store for `/org` **and** `/workspace`, mounted by every AWS host. Nobody has measured whether a metadata-heavy workload is viable on it. The epic records EFS-for-AWS-hosts as having *"no unknowns blocking it"* — that is true of the experiments run so far and **not** true of this assumption.

This is now the highest-value unmeasured thing in `chatticus-fbae4e`, because it is the only remaining question that can invalidate D1, and D1 is the foundation the rest of the design rests on.

## Why `9af381` Phase A0 does not answer it

A0 measured a **WAN** path against **nfs-ganesha in Docker** and reported that `actimeo` made no difference to warm `git status` (1743x / 1629x / 1637x / 1640x / 1649x across actimeo 1–300s — flat).

Two confounds prevent generalising that to in-VPC EFS:

1. **The workload self-invalidates.** Each timed iteration in `spikes/nfs-wan-netem-9af381/scripts/lib-bench.sh` `run_ops()` runs `git status` → `git checkout bench-a && git checkout bench-b` → `stat` sweep. The checkout rewrites the tree every pass, so the next `git status` revalidates regardless of `actimeo`. The experiment did not test whether a long `actimeo` helps a warm, read-mostly tree — it tested a tree under continuous mutation, where cache invalidation is expected.
2. **Ganesha is not EFS.** A0's own LAN control shows a ~13x tax versus local disk at 0.2 ms RTT, which is server overhead, not network. Its own summary says *"do not call that EFS."* A userspace NFS server may also return weaker change attributes than the Linux client needs to trust its cache — exactly the mechanism under test.

So A0's WAN verdict stands (32 s is catastrophic under any reading, and real agent workloads do write files). Its **mechanism** claim does not.

## What is actually at stake

Rough arithmetic on the ~976-file fixture, in-VPC:

| If | Then |
|---|---|
| The attribute cache works on real EFS (proper NFSv4.1 change attributes) | Warm runs collapse toward local. D1 holds. Build EFS. |
| Per-file round trips dominate | ~0.5–1 ms EFS metadata latency × ~1000 files ≈ **0.5–1 s vs 0.02 s local = 25–50x**, over the agreed threshold. D1 fails for AWS hosts, and the answer reverts to the data-shape split (`/org` on EFS, hot tree on local disk) that `fbae4e` considered and rejected. |

Both are plausible. Nothing on the board distinguishes them.

## Method

Deliberately the production configuration, not a lab analogue.

- One EFS filesystem in the Chatticus VPC (`vpc-0c5a0f0ca21e2afdd`), General Purpose mode, mount target in a private subnet.
- One EC2 instance in that VPC, `amazon-efs-utils` mount.
- Same operation set and fixture as A0 so the numbers are comparable.
- **Critical difference from A0: a read-only repeat loop.** Run `git status` N times with no mutation between iterations, to isolate the attribute-cache question the A0 confound obscured. Then, separately, run the A0 mutating sequence for a realistic-workload number.
- Control: same operations on the instance's local EBS.
- Capture `nfsstat -c` / mountstats RPC deltas per run — RPC counts explain whether the cache is being used, which wall time alone cannot.
- Sweep `actimeo` as A0 did, but only the read-only loop makes that sweep meaningful.

## Thresholds

Reuse the agreed table, against local EBS on the same instance: within ~3x proceed; 3–10x marginal, reopen the data-shape split; over 10x, D1 fails for `/workspace` and `/org`-only EFS becomes the design.

## Cost

An EFS filesystem for a few hours costs pennies; one EC2 instance-hour costs cents. Half a day including teardown.

**Run this before any EFS CDK is written.** It is cheap, and it is the one result that could make that CDK the wrong thing to build.

## Done when

Read-only and mutating numbers are recorded against the threshold table with RPC counts, and `chatticus-fbae4e` D1 is either confirmed for `/workspace` or narrowed to `/org`.

comments.text: Composer 2.5 planning in-VPC EFS vs EBS. Worktree to be `/tmp/chatticus-3d5357-efs-invpc` on `spike/efs-invpc-3d5357`. Chatticus VPC `vpc-0c5a0f0ca21e2afdd` currently has **only public subnets** (`subnet-06c4e78bf06400f26` 1a, `subnet-0b7f7c7be05091111` 1b) — no private subnet to put a mount target in. Plan must name that and not invent a NAT/private tier. No tunnel. No Kanbus EFS. Tear the experiment FS/EC2 down after. Implementation not authorized until plan review.

comments.text: Plan authorized with amendments: SSM-only EC2 in `subnet-06c4e78bf06400f26` (no private/NAT), throwaway GP EFS, destroy-on-failure, no S3 bucket, no Kanbus FS, no tunnel. Read-only `git status` loop is the cache test; mutating A0 sequence is a separate table. Worktree `/tmp/chatticus-3d5357-efs-invpc` on `spike/efs-invpc-3d5357`.

comments.text: In-VPC numbers are in [#311](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Chatticus/pull/311). Mutating A0 vs local EBS: **23–54×** (`ratio_overall`) — **D1 fails for `/workspace` (>10×)**. Read-only warm `git status`: **~10–12×** EBS; RPC 203 → ~131 (−35%), not a near-zero cache. `actimeo=1` thrashes. Throwaway FS `fs-028e92bee71335473` and all spike EC2/SG/IAM are gone; Kanbus EFS untouched; Computers `desiredCount` still 0. Reviewing before merge. Do not write EFS CDK.
